rounds.proof_sketch: n = blockIdx.x where grid.x = batch_size = 16. Thus n ∈ [0, 15]. Original: n >= 16 → always false. Mutated: n > 16 → always false. Both expressions evaluate identically for n ∈ [0, 15]. The difference (n == 16) is unreachable since blockIdx.x maxes at batch_size - 1 = 15.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the early-exit condition from 'n >= batch_size' to 'n > batch_size'. However, the kernel launch sets grid.x = batch_size, meaning blockIdx.x (assigned to n) ranges from 0 to batch_size-1 (i.e., 0 to 15 for the fixed batch_size=16). Within this range, both 'n >= 16' and 'n > 16' evaluate to false for all valid thread indices. The only distinguishing case would be n == batch_size, but this value is architecturally unreachable given the CUDA grid launch configuration. No input tensor values can affect thread indices, making this mutation semantically equivalent under the fixed-shape contract.
rounds.kill_strategy: This mutant is unkillable under the fixed-shape contract. The mutation only affects behavior when n == batch_size, but the kernel launch configuration (grid.x = batch_size) ensures blockIdx.x never reaches that value. Killing would require either changing batch_size or modifying kernel launch parameters, both of which violate the testing contract.
rounds.recommendations: Boundary guard mutations in CUDA kernels that check thread/block indices against dimension parameters are often unkillable when the grid dimensions exactly match the work dimensions. For better mutation testing coverage, consider: (1) testing with configurations where grid dimensions exceed work dimensions, (2) adding explicit fuzz testing of kernel launch parameters, or (3) marking such boundary-guard mutations as equivalent when the launch configuration mathematically prevents the boundary from being reached.
